# OUSD(R&E) Developmental Test and Evaluation of AI-Enabled Systems Guidebook

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Office of the Director, Developmental Test, Evaluation, and Assessments (DTEA); Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering (OUSD(R&E)) |
| **Kind** | Guidebook (DoD T&E community guidance, consensus-based) |
| **Status** | February 2025 edition. DOPSR Case # 25-T-1195. Describes itself as reflecting "the T&E community's current consensus," expected to need updates as the field moves (Executive Summary, p.iii). |
| **Where to get it** | Public: cto.mil/dtea; Distribution Statement A, approved for public release, distribution unlimited. Public copy, confirmed anonymously off-network on 2026-10-26: `https://www.cto.mil/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/TE_of_AIES_Guidebook-Feb-2025-1.pdf` |
| **Binds whom** | DoD government test teams planning and executing developmental test and evaluation (DT&E) for AI-enabled components, applications, and systems (Executive Summary, p.iii) — guidance for DoD programs, not a NASA/JPL document. |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** The DoD T&E community's own AI-specific
guidebook — a useful point of comparison for what an AI-focused *test and evaluation* guidance document
looks like, as distinct from NASA's software-assurance-process documents (our reading).

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.**
- States its purpose as providing "technically sound, consensus-based guidance" to support government
  test teams in planning and executing DT&E for AI-enabled components, applications, and systems, and
  in delivering insights to decision makers during AIES development and deployment (Executive Summary,
  p.iii, paraphrase/partial quote).
- Explicitly frames AI as a dual concern for test teams: AI as the system under test (SUT), and AI as a
  tool used to execute tests.
- A text search of the public PDF finds roughly 65 occurrences of "artificial intelligence"/"machine learning,"
  consistent with the title — the whole document is AI-focused, unlike the general T&E guidebooks in
  this same series (see companion pages).

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** No NASA document is dedicated to AI-specific T&E planning in this way;
compares to `../documents/NPR_7120.5F.md` (program/project management, including T&E planning
generally) and `../documents/NASA-STD-7009B.md` (model credibility) (our reading, comparison only).
